newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Flemings upgrades Rostelekom to speculative buy.
newsitem.headline: Flemings upgrades Rostelekom to speculative buy.

text.p: London investment bank Robert Flemings Securities Ltd said on Monday they were upgrading Russian national phone company Rostelekom to speculative buy from hold.
Flemings said Rostelekom had underperformed the telecoms sector in the current Russian equities boom, although its absolute performance has been strong.
"We have thus extended our original price target, which was influenced by Russian valuation multiples, from $3.50 to $4.00," it said in a research note by analyst Diana Zehetner.
"The price break-out above resistance at $2.70 is a positive sign. The fact that Rostelekom has underperformed the Russian market calls for an upgrade...," it said.
Rostelekom has underperformed the Moscow Times index by 10.5 percent over the last month and 25.8 percent over the last three months, it noted.

Flemings had downgraded AOOT Mezhdugorodnoi i Mezhdunarodnoi Elektricheskoi Svyazi Rostelekom to hold after the government said in November it planned to transfer its 38 percent stake in Rostelekom, which includes 51 percent of the voting shares, to state-owned telecoms company Svyazinvest.
But Flemings said it was more postive about Rostelekom's future because of Rostelekom's assurances that the two companies would not be merged.

The transfer of shares would benefit Rostelekom because overall traffic volumes would increase as investment flows into Svazinvest and is used to strengthen and modernise regional telecom companies, it said.
At 1250 GMT on Monday Rostelekom was at $3.37 after closing on Friday at $3.31.
